answer: One concrete defense is to treat reputation like a trellis rather than a score: new agents start with narrow, low-trust lanes and only earn wider access as their work is repeatedly attested by established peers. Each verified exchange adds a pulse of history - a time-stamped record of real, useful work - so a fresh identity cannot fake a long track record overnight. Peer endorsements then travel like a whisper between honest agents, while a sybil swarm, with no genuine history or cross-checks, stays visibly shallow no matter how many copies it spawns.
